findings.title: whatThe51FixturesCover identifies the 51 authored corpus fixtures with the 48 rideless schema-derived map keys. The identification is false against live bytes on two independent counts, and it assigns a producer to 45 of those 48 keys that v14 assigns elsewhere, which FG-6 makes report-invalid.
findings.theClaim: v5 whatThe51FixturesCover opens: 'The 51 authored exact-byte fixtures recorded at D-106 are the produced rideless schema-derived keys (48 of them; the 5 rided schema-derived keys are not among the 51). They execute on every matrix cell, not only clean.' The second sentence is the correct v4 repair. The first sentence is the defect.

countOne.issue: The two names live in different namespaces and do not intersect at all.
countOne.evidence: component-manifest-fixture-corpus.v6.json carries authoredCount 51 and an authored[] array of 51 objects whose ids are TC-ACCEPT.minimal, TC-ACCEPT.maximal, TC-ACCEPT.approved-exception, TC-DUP.different-provenance, TC-NAME.reserved-root, TC-PATH.dotdot, TC-SIG.unsigned, TC-BYTE-EXACT.digest-recompute and so on. v14's fixtureMemberMap keys are TC-ACCEPT.0 through TC-ACCEPT.5, TC-NAME.0 through TC-NAME.11 with the .alias, .shadow, .4.after, .4.inside and .5.unknown arms, TC-PATH.0 through TC-PATH.12, and so on. Measured by set intersection: zero of the 51 corpus ids is a key of the 80-key map, and all 48 of the 48 keys v5 enumerates are unmatched by any corpus id. The cardinalities also differ, 51 against 48, which the sentence acknowledges parenthetically without reconciling. No join between the two namespaces is recorded in v5, in corpus v6, or in v14.

countTwo.issue: v14 assigns exactly one producer per key, and only 3 of the 48 are hand-authored.
countTwo.evidence: v14 fixtureGeneration FG-1 states 'Every fixtureMemberMap.members key maps to exactly one producer and exactly one expected outcome'. Counted from live bytes across the exact 48 keys v5 enumerates: fixtureGenerator 31, S-3-EMIT 8, behavioral-harness 6, authored-exact-bytes 3. The three whose producer is authored-exact-bytes are TC-BYTE-EXACT.2, TC-NAME.4.after and TC-NAME.4.inside. The other 45 are assigned elsewhere.
countTwo.whyItBites: v14 conformanceReport.shape.fixtureClassCoverage states that 'Class-wide stand-ins, missing keys, duplicate keys, or alternative producers are report-invalid', and FG-6 states that 'Report validation rejects a fixtureClassCoverage that is missing any fixtureMemberMap.members key, duplicates a key, uses a class-wide stand-in, or records a producer/ride other than fixtureMemberMap.members[memberKey].' FG-3 adds that hand-authoring the exact-byte corpus 'is lawful evidence that the classes exist. It is not an adapter run.' The 8 S-3-EMIT keys are adapter emissions by definition, so the authored corpus cannot be their producer even in principle.

findings.operativeBite: v5 correctly requires all 48 rideless schema-derived keys to stand produced with {path, sha256} on each of the twelve reports, and then tells the implementer that the 51 authored fixtures are those keys and execute on every matrix cell. Following that instruction records the hand-authored corpus as the producer for 45 of 48 keys across 12 reports — 540 member standings carrying a producer other than fixtureMemberMap.members[memberKey] — which FG-6 rejects and the coverage shape calls report-invalid. This is the same defect class as CLAUDE-G15H-V2-SF1, V3-SF1 and V4-SF1: a pass condition that admits a report-invalid fixtureClassCoverage. It now arrives through the producer clause rather than through missing keys.
findings.regressionNote: This is introduced by v5. v4's sentence read 'The 51 authored exact-byte fixtures recorded at D-106 are DR-103 admission classes (TC-NAME, TC-PATH, TC-ACCEPT, TC-DUP, TC-CLOSURE, TC-BYTE-EXACT, TC-SIG, TC-METADATA-ONLY). They supply the clean-cell portion of members 1 and 2.' That was a class-level supply claim and was true — the corpus classes do equal the map-key families, verified by set equality on the family prefixes. v5 rewrote it into a key-level identity claim with a count in order to carry the every-cell repair, and the identity is false while the repair it carries is correct.
notRescuedBy: closedMap does not rescue it. closedMap correctly enumerates the 48 keys and their standing, and says nothing about who produces them; it neither repeats nor contradicts the identity claim, so the only statement in the artifact about what supplies those keys is the false one.

EV-1.suppliedBy does not rescue it. It was correctly rewritten to 'The 48 rideless schema-derived keys, AT-1-ASSEMBLY, and AT-8 / all seventeen AT-ARCHIVE-* keys on every cell', which names the keys without claiming a producer. That makes whatThe51FixturesCover the sole producer statement, and it is unqualified.

executesWhenRun does not rescue it. It still reads 'The 51 authored exact-byte fixtures recorded at D-106, plus the AT-1..AT-8 / CI / LV classes specified above', which reinforces rather than limits the identification.

The parenthetical '(48 of them; the 5 rided schema-derived keys are not among the 51)' does not rescue it. It reconciles which keys are excluded, not the 51-to-48 mismatch, and it does not touch the producer question at all.
findings.remedyShape: Restore a supply claim in place of an identity claim and keep the every-cell repair. A correct sentence would say that the 51 authored corpus fixtures are hand-authored evidence for the eight DR-103 admission classes under FG-3, that they are not themselves fixtureMemberMap keys and carry no producer standing, and that the 48 rideless schema-derived keys are produced on every cell by the producer v14 records for each — fixtureGenerator for 31, S-3-EMIT for 8, behavioral-harness for 6, authored-exact-bytes for 3 — with FG-6 forbidding any other producer. If a join between the corpus ids and the map keys is intended, it has to be authored and independently reviewed rather than asserted, and that authoring is not this artifact's to do. This reviewer authors no join, no fixture bytes, and no obligation text.
findings.gradeRationale: Graded SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker because the artifact binds nothing, applies nothing, is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED at DO-NOT-SEAL with gates2and3HoldForDR103 false, and because the closedMap work it delivers is correct and complete. Graded SHOULD-FIX and not advisory because the sentence is false against live bytes, is the artifact's only statement about what supplies 48 of its 80 required keys, and drives a coverage array the pinned contract rejects.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: v5 lands CLAUDE-G15H-V4-SF1 completely and correctly. The new closedMap block reproduces v14's closed map exactly — 80 keys set-equal with zero missing, extra or duplicate; every section count correct; the arithmetic correct; all ten ride strings and expected tokens byte-exact, including the three distinct ride spellings among the schema-derived five — and reportUnit.eachReport ends the v4 produced-versus-blocked ambiguity outright. All three cells now carry 80 of 80 map keys. AT-7's ride ID-DEP-P7, which this reviewer flagged without charging at v3 and v4, is now named. V1-SF1, V2-SF1 and V3-SF1 all remain landed. Every mechanical check is clean — subject unmoved at 6ad4eb07 and 0444, thirteen of thirteen cited digests equal live bytes, file 08 pin equal to live, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, prohibition scan clean. One SHOULD-FIX stands, introduced by this revision: whatThe51FixturesCover now states that the 51 authored corpus fixtures are the 48 rideless schema-derived keys. Zero of the 51 corpus ids is a map key and only 3 of the 48 carry producer authored-exact-bytes, so the sentence assigns 45 keys a producer v14 assigns elsewhere, which FG-6 and the coverage shape declare report-invalid.
